summary: Validated the service photos feature end-to-end. Backend (11/11 pytest tests pass in test_service_photos.py): admin can POST /api/files with a real PNG; POST /api/services persists photos=[{file_id,filename,content_type}] and GET /api/services returns them; PUT /api/services clears photos; services without photos still work (default [] on both POST/GET); user is 403 on POST /files, POST/PUT/DELETE /services, but 200 on GET /services (cost stripped) and GET /api/files//download. Frontend admin (/repairs): opening the service form shows 'Foto (Dokumentasi)' with 'Tambah Foto' (add-photo-button) and hidden input (service-photo-input); selecting a .txt shows 'Hanya berkas gambar yang diperbolehkan' and selecting a >2MB PNG shows 'Ukuran foto melebihi 2 MB', neither adds a thumbnail; uploading a small 20x20 PNG shows a success toast + form-photo-0 with remove-photo-0; saving persists the photo so services-table row shows 'photos-service-' button in the 'Foto' column (column order confirmed Tanggal/Mesin/Jenis/Teknisi/Bukti TTD/Foto/Biaya/Status/Aksi); clicking it opens photo-gallery-dialog with gallery-photo-0 that actually renders (naturalWidth=20 via same-origin to /api/files//download); clicking the gallery thumb opens photo-lightbox; opening the form on an existing service and clicking form-photo-0 also opens the lightbox; clicking remove-photo-0 then Simpan persists the removal (row's photos button disappears). Frontend operator: no add-service-button / edit / delete buttons on /repairs, Biaya column hidden (headers only ['Tanggal','Mesin','Jenis','Teknisi','Bukti TTD','Foto','Status','Aksi']); can still open photos-service-, gallery, and lightbox (naturalWidth=20) — view/preview-only, no remove buttons present. BAP PDF (pdf-service-) button still present on all rows.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py now ~977 lines - still exceeds 700-line guideline; services/files/schedules should be split into separate routers.

ServicePhoto has no server-side validation that content_type starts with 'image/' or that file_id references an existing /api/files record; a malicious admin could attach arbitrary file_ids (low risk since admin-only, but worth asserting).

/api/files/{id}/download sends Content-Disposition: attachment; this does not block rendering (confirmed), but adding a sibling 'inline' endpoint or branching on an ?inline=1 param would be cleaner for the gallery use-case.
/api/files DELETE only soft-deletes (is_deleted=True) but the underlying object in storage is never removed; over time this bloats storage. Consider a background purge for soft-deleted files.

Repairs.js photo URL is built as `${API}/files//download` and relies on withCredentials cookies on the tag. Works today because /api is same-origin via the preview proxy; if frontend/backend are split onto different origins the images will stop rendering (CORS does not help ). Document this assumption or proxy /api in production too.
Repairs.js is ~337 lines but contains both admin and viewer UI with lots of inline JSX; splitting Gallery + Lightbox into their own components would improve readability and testability.
